reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: AI eroding trust, outpacing governance
themes.definition: AI framed as a monumental, fast-moving disruption that outpaces existing governance and makes building trust in technology the central challenge.
themes.inclusion: Include passages emphasizing the speed/scale of AI disruption, lost trust in technology, or inadequacy of existing rules.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages focused only on specific harms like weapons or disinformation.
themes.boundary_cases: If the passage moves to calls for global rules, also code AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: It appears to be moving far too fast for anybody, let alone governments, to manage to keep pace.
I am afraid that in our digital age, part of the problem of losing trust lies with science and technology.

themes.label: Collective global rules for AI
themes.definition: Calls for collectively set global rules on AI, since no state can manage it alone, including governance that balances opportunity and risk with private sector commitment.
themes.inclusion: Include calls for global/international AI rules or collective governance involving all actors.
themes.exclusion: Exclude statements that only describe AI's speed without a governance call.
themes.boundary_cases: References to the Global Digital Compact or SG advisory body also get AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: acknowledging that the rules need to be set globally and they need to be stuck to even as they develop
We need to find a way to govern the development of new technologies, including artificial intelligence

themes.label: Human-centric, rights-based lifecycle approach
themes.definition: A human-centric and human rights-based approach across the full technology life cycle.
themes.inclusion: Include calls for human-centric or rights-based AI approaches.
themes.exclusion: Exclude general trust concerns without a rights/values framing.
themes.boundary_cases: Appeals to 'the right values' underpinning action are borderline; include only when values are human-centred.

examples.quote: The answer should be a humancentric and human rights-based approach to the full life cycle of technologies

themes.label: SG advisory body and Global Digital Compact
themes.definition: Support for UN AI processes such as the SG's high-level advisory body on AI and the Global Digital Compact.
themes.inclusion: Include mentions of UN AI bodies or the Global Digital Compact.
themes.boundary_cases: Split passages that complete a sentence about the SG advisory body count.

examples.quote: I applaud the Secretary- General’s resolve to form a high-level advisory body on
The Global Digital Compact should be centred on that notion.

themes.label: AI useful but dangerous
themes.definition: AI explicitly framed as both useful and dangerous.
themes.inclusion: Include explicit dual framings of AI.
themes.boundary_cases: Governance that 'does not impede opportunities and does not put us at risk' also qualifies.

examples.quote: Artificial intelligence can be useful, but it can also be dangerous.

value.rationale: Slovenia and Malta both tie AI to a crisis of trust; Malta stresses AI's unprecedented speed outrunning governance and the need for global rules, while Slovenia calls for human-rights-based governance through the SG advisory body and Global Digital Compact.
